focus_area_title: Implement "TeamSTEPPSÂ®, a teamwork system that offers a powerful solution to improving collaboration and communication"
content_text_body:
TeamSTEPPSÂ® is a teamwork system developed by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality and the U.S. Department of Defense specifically for healthcare in the mid-2000s. It is designed to offer a powerful solution to improving collaboration and communication. 

### Why is it important?

Poor communication and teamwork are some of the leading causes of medical errors and patient safety events. In fact, a review of reports from the Joint Commission reveals that communication failures were implicated at the root of over 70 percent of sentinel events. It is important to regularly evaluate how teams within your organization are communicating and supporting each other to improve patient safety. 

On the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality's (AHRQ's) website there is robust information regarding TeamSTEPPSÂ®. Below are some of the main modules of the training and a brief summary for each.  For more information on the training and to assess whether or not your organization is ready for this, visit [https://www.ahrq.gov/teamstepps/readiness/index.html](https://www.ahrq.gov/teamstepps/readiness/index.html).
 
### Considering your Team Structure

The goal here is for individuals to understand the benefits of team structure in teamwork, define the term "team," and understand the team's structure and how multiple teams interact together to provide great care.  Finally, the role of patients and families in the care team is also discussed.  

### Communication

Arguably one of the most important modules in the training the goal here is to convey to learners how critical communication is to team performance, define effective communication, and challenges to effective communication. Furthermore, communication strategies to reduce miscommunications and errors are discussed such as SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation), Call-Outs (used to convey critical information), Check-Back's (strategy used to confirm that information was properly received), and Handoffs (Communication strategies such as I-PASS when a patient is being transferred to another shift or unit).  There are also opportunities in the TeamSTEPPSÂ® training to practice these skills.   

### Leading Teams

The goal of this module is for learners to understand the characteristics of effective leadership, the importance of role-modeling behaviors, and a leader's role in conflict resolution. Learners will also learn the tools leaders have to lead their teams such as huddles, briefs, and debriefs, and they'll have the opportunity to apply these tools in clinical scenarios.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           

### Situation Monitoring

The concept of situation monitoring - or team members understanding what is happening around them - is discussed and how it fits into effective teamwork and safety. Learners will understand how situation monitoring allows for team members to adapt and respond effectively to changing situations, how leaders support situation monitoring, and how individuals communicating their perception of the situation routinely to their teammates is critical to proper care.  

### Mutual Support

The goal here is for individuals to understand how mutual support affects team performance, the strategies that help foster mutual support amongst teams (e.g., task assistance, feedback), identify tools to encourage mutual support and discuss ways to reduce conflict.
